findings.defective_text: (sweep: 2 verses, the koh-amar formula within chs 41-43, both divine-owned), the book's ordinary marker for a new divine
findings.byte_evidence: sweep.py --skel כה אמר returns 48 verses book-wide; the chs 41-43 window holds FOUR, not two: oshb:Isa.42.5 כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה, oshb:Isa.43.1 וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙, oshb:Isa.43.14 כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה, oshb:Isa.43.16 כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (all byte tier, each against its own verse). The device inventory's koh_amar block lists the same four and classes all four divine-owned, so 'both divine-owned' is short by two. The companion formulation in P12-001's boundary_rationale ('one of only two divine-owned koh-amar frames in this run of oracles ... (sweep: 2 verses)') names no window at all, and its own part-mates contradict it: P12-002's boundary_rationale calls web:Isa.43.14 'the fresh koh-amar frame naming the Redeemer' and P12-004's opens 'A second fresh koh-amar frame ... at web:Isa.43.16'.
findings.proposed_cure: Restate P11-012's digit as '(sweep: 4 verses, the koh-amar formula within chs 41-43 -- oshb:Isa.42.5, oshb:Isa.43.1, oshb:Isa.43.14, oshb:Isa.43.16, all four divine-owned)' and give P12-001's 'only two' its actual window (42:5 through this row's own span) or the same four-verse digit.

findings.checklist_class: 1 repair-installed unswept universal; 6 E-03 lens (digit re-collated against the bytes)
findings.defective_text: the second member's opener, הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ (oshb:Isa.51.4, tier: byte), is unique at every tier (byte, accent_stripped and skeleton alike: 1 verse). This span's own closing verse carries שָׂשׂ
findings.byte_evidence: sweep.py --heb on the 51:4 opener spliced from the verse bytes, הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ, returns byte 1 / accent_stripped 4 / skeleton 4. Word-bound the same skeleton stands at THREE verses -- oshb:Isa.28.23 הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ, oshb:Isa.34.1 הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ, oshb:Isa.51.4 הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ -- and the tool's substring arm reaches a fourth verse, oshb:Isa.49.1, on its vav-prefixed token וְהַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ, a verse this same part's P14-001 quotes in full in its own boundary_rationale. Only the byte tier is unique; 'unique at every tier ... 1 verse' is false at accent_stripped and skeleton alike. The same row's other digit in the same sentence -- שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ byte-identical at exactly 3 verses book-wide (4 at accent_stripped and skeleton) -- re-derives exactly, which isolates the haqshivu clause as the defective one.
findings.proposed_cure: Restate to 'byte-unique to its own verse (1 verse) but standing at 3 verses word-bound from accent_stripped tier down (oshb:Isa.28.23, oshb:Isa.34.1, oshb:Isa.51.4)'.

findings.checklist_class: 2 warrant substitution weakening the row's own evidence; 4 repair-narration register bleed
findings.defective_text: since a respan is a boss-adoption proposal and would fall under the whole-chapter medium_low confidence cap.
findings.byte_evidence: The clause closes strongest_rejected_alternative and supplies the ONLY stated ground for not adopting the disclosed larger-chapter reading -- a process ground, not a textual one, while the row's own boundary_rationale already carries the textual ground (the 62:9|62:10 turn from the charge laid on the watchmen to the highway-preparation summons, עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים, oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier). Register sweep over all 223 rows: 'boss', 'respan' and 'adoption proposal' each occur in exactly ONE row corpus-wide, this one; the five other rows that reference the whole-chapter cap (P03-014, P05-005, P05-009, P09-001, P09-005) all keep it in device_notes as 'the campaign's whole-chapter cap/ceiling' with no actor name attached. The row's own span (Isa.62.10-Isa.62.12) is not a whole chapter, so the cap is not even operative on it.
findings.proposed_cure: Strike the actor/rule clause and close the sentence on the textual reason already argued in the row's own boundary_rationale -- the content turn at web:Isa.62.9|Isa.62.10 -- so the rival is refused on the bytes rather than on adoption procedure.

findings.checklist_class: 1 repair-installed universal without digits; 6 E-03 lens (ruling-text fact propagated into a row)
findings.defective_text: The light-and-rising root that closes this row's own front-seam neighbor, וּמִמִּזְרַח שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ (oshb:Isa.59.19), runs on past this row's own rear seam through זָרָֽח (oshb:Isa.60.1, byte tier), יִזְרַ֣ח (oshb:Isa.60.2, byte tier), and זַרְחֵֽךְ (oshb:Isa.60.3, byte tier) -- four consecutive verses straddling the seam undisclose
findings.byte_evidence: Two byte-checkable facts in one disclosure are wrong. (a) POSITION IN SPAN: the row's span is Isa.59.15-Isa.59.21, so oshb:Isa.59.19 is INTERIOR to it (verse 5 of 7); this row's front-seam neighbour is oshb:Isa.59.14. (b) POSITION IN VERSE: oshb:Isa.59.19 reads וְיִֽירְא֤וּ מִֽמַּעֲרָב֙ אֶת שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּמִמִּזְרַח שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ אֶת כְּבוֹד֑וֹ כִּֽי יָב֤וֹא כַנָּהָר֙ צָ֔ר ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה נֹ֥סְסָה בֽוֹ -- the cited run וּמִמִּזְרַח שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ stands at tokens 6-7 of 17 (mid-verse), and the verse closes on נֹ֥סְסָה בֽוֹ, so the run does not 'close' that verse. (c) COUNT-OBJECT: the four cited sites are oshb:Isa.59.19, oshb:Isa.60.1, oshb:Isa.60.2, oshb:Isa.60.3 -- oshb:Isa.59.20 and oshb:Isa.59.21 intervene, so they are not 'four consecutive verses'.
findings.proposed_cure: Restate as 'the light-and-rising root standing mid-verse inside this row's own span at oshb:Isa.59.19 runs on past this row's own rear seam through oshb:Isa.60.1, oshb:Isa.60.2 and oshb:Isa.60.3', dropping the front-seam-neighbour label, the 'closes' verb and the consecutive-verses count.

findings.checklist_class: 2 warrant substitution contradicting the row's own evidence (tier misstatement repeated in two fields)
findings.defective_text: a pairing that differs at byte and at accent-stripped tier and meets only at skeleton tier, where it stands in 22 verses book-wide
findings.byte_evidence: collate.py --json, both directions, on the two runs spliced from their own verses -- אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.60.16) and אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.60.22) -- returns tier accent_stripped for BOTH, not skeleton: the two differ only in cantillation (mahpakh/pashta against merkha/tipcha), and isa_lib.strip_accents makes them equal. sweep.py --heb gives byte 9 / accent_stripped 22 / skeleton 22 for the first form and byte 7 / accent_stripped 22 / skeleton 22 for the second, so the 22-verse digit is right but is reached one tier higher than the row states. The same misstatement is repeated in strongest_rejected_alternative ('the echo itself is a skeleton-tier match only'). The same part gets the analogous case right at P17-004 ('differ only in cantillation' -> accent_stripped), which isolates this row's clause.
findings.proposed_cure: Change both fields to 'differs at byte tier and meets from accent_stripped tier down, where it stands in 22 verses book-wide' -- the tier-disclosure standard requires the tier collate actually returns.

findings.byte_evidence: The run quoted on the oshb:Isa.37.35 side is the WHOLE verse, וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי, but only its first four tokens recur. collate.py: that full run against oshb:Isa.38.6 returns tier NONE; sweep.py --heb on the full run returns 1 verse at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton alike. The four-token clause spliced from oshb:Isa.38.6, וְגַנּוֹתִ֖י עַל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּֽאת, is what carries the claim: byte 1 / accent_stripped 1 / skeleton 2 (oshb:Isa.37.35, oshb:Isa.38.6) -- so 'sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier' is true of the clause and false of the run as quoted, which overshoots by five tokens (לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי) that appear nowhere in oshb:Isa.38.6. The seam partner P10-009 states the same device correctly, naming the recurrence object as the defend-this-city CLAUSE and quoting only the oshb:Isa.38.6 side.
findings.proposed_cure: Cut the oshb:Isa.37.35 splice back to its first four tokens so the quoted extent matches the 2-verse skeleton-tier digit and the seam partner's formulation.

P14-016's span closes at web:Isa.51.20, so a mark keyed to (i.e. terminating) oshb:Isa.51.21 falls one verse PAST that close and corroborates the 51:21|51:22 division, not this row's 51:20|51:21 close; the asserted symmetry with oshb:Isa.51.16 does not hold, because that mark does terminate the verse immediately before P14-016's onset. findings.defective_text: P11-007 device_notes: 'a catchword undisclosed elsewhere' | P11-008 device_notes: 'a catchword undisclosed elsewhere' | P16-001 device_notes: 'this row's own front seam carries an undisclosed cross-seam echo' | P18-008 boundary_rationale: 'an unmarked, undisclosed front-seam continuity'
findings.byte_evidence: Three seam pairs in this half each carry a disclosure-STATE claim that the row on the other side of the same seam falsifies. (1) oshb:Isa.40.31|oshb:Isa.41.1: P11-007 and P11-008 BOTH call יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ (oshb:Isa.41.1) / יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ (oshb:Isa.40.31) 'a catchword undisclosed elsewhere', each being the other's disclosure. (2) oshb:Isa.55.13|oshb:Isa.56.1: P16-001 calls לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת 'an undisclosed cross-seam echo' while its seam partner P15-006 discloses the identical pair WITH digits ('byte tier in exactly two verses book-wide ... its consonantal skeleton reaches three, adding oshb:Isa.48.19' -- re-derived here as byte 2 / skeleton 3). (3) oshb:Isa.65.16|oshb:Isa.65.17: P18-007 cites 'two undisclosed cross-seam ties' and P18-008 'an unmarked, undisclosed front-seam continuity' for the same הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת tie (byte 2 verses, re-derived). NOTE the qualifier is an established corpus idiom (17 sites over 7 parts, incl. P01/P08 outside this half), so the class is a scoping defect, not a fabrication.
findings.proposed_cure: Scope the qualifier to what it actually asserts ('not surfaced by the English rendering') or drop it on the second-stated side of each pair, so two neighbours never both claim a shared device is undisclosed.

findings.checklist_class: WARN triage: the 4 citation_sweep prose_dual_warns in this half
findings.defective_text: Hebrew quote in row.device_notes/boundary_rationale binds to a K/Q verse with no ketiv/qere disclosure in-field (oshb:Isa.37.30 x2, oshb:Isa.42.24, oshb:Isa.44.24).
findings.byte_evidence: Substantively safe -- every quoted run stands clear of its verse's K/Q token pair. oshb:Isa.37.30 K/Q = ואכול וְאִכְל֥וּ at tokens 16-17 of 18, quoted run וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת at tokens 1-3. oshb:Isa.42.24 K/Q = למשוסה לִמְשִׁסָּ֧ה at tokens 3-4 of 19, P12-001 quotes יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל at tokens 5-6. oshb:Isa.44.24 K/Q = מי אתי מֵאִתִּֽי at tokens 16-18 of 18, P12-010 quotes גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ at token 4. What is missing is only the one-clause in-field note the corpus itself uses at P16-002 ('the quoted span begins after the varying token pair') and P16-004 ('not through Isa.57.19's own K/Q-flagged token pair'). Dispositioned genuine but minor: a disclosure gap, not a byte defect.
findings.proposed_cure: Add the corpus's own one-clause in-field note to each of the four fields, stating that the quoted run stands clear of that verse's ketiv/qere token pair (single-witness apparatus).

findings.defective_text: P13-006 device_notes: 'argued in the rejected-alternative field above rather than here' | P14-013: 'named in the rationale field' | P14-018: 'disclosed in the rationale field' | P14-021: 'spliced at byte tier in the rationale field'
findings.byte_evidence: Register sweep over all 223 rows: the pattern '<name> field' occurs at exactly FIVE sites corpus-wide, four of them in P14 (P14-013, P14-018, P14-020, P14-021) and one in P13 (P13-006) -- a localized cluster, not an established idiom like the 25-site 'previous/next row' phrasing. P13-006's is the clearest instance because it adds file-order positioning ('the field above'). The register purge bars cross-field references and file-order talk in any row field; every one of these clauses is removable without loss, since the fact referred to is already verse-anchored in the field being pointed at.
findings.proposed_cure: Replace each field pointer with the verse anchor it stands for (or delete the clause), e.g. P13-006's 'argued in the rejected-alternative field above rather than here' -> 'the two declined summons onsets at web:Isa.48.14 and web:Isa.48.16 are not argued here'.
